summary: Branch forwarder TTL skew causes OCSP timeouts and stalled model shard downloads
description:
Issue summary: After a network change at the customer's branch office, the customer's DNS forwarders began returning inconsistent TTLs for the VPCE and artifact-host A records. This caused Redwood control-plane components to continue using stale IPs and defer re-resolution longer than expected, leading to repeated OCSP lookup timeouts and stalled model shard downloads for the customer's private deployment.

Impact: Production inference on several routes experienced elevated model pull latency and intermittent 502/504 errors between 2026-03-12T08:40Z and 2026-03-12T11:20Z. Customer reports failed artifact fetches for large model shards and degraded end-user latency.

Environment: Private deployment (Fintegrity Solutions), prod - eu-west-1, VPCE-backed control plane and artifact S3 endpoint via a presigned range workflow.

Observed symptoms:
- Agent logs show repeated "ocsp: lookup timeout" and "artifact fetch retry" messages.
- Control-plane healthchecks repeatedly retried to the same IP for the artifact endpoint for periods matching the larger TTL.
- Wire captures show alternating A answers with TTLs of 30s and 1200s from different forwarders.
- Customers' forwarder cache did not respect negative/low TTLs and served stale records for longer than expected.

Steps to reproduce (from customer env):
1) run: dig +nocmd +noall +answer artifact-eu-west.example-s3.internal @10.10.2.2 (branch forwarder)
2) run the same dig against a different forwarder (10.10.3.2) and compare TTL fields
3) run tcpdump on agent during a model pull and observe OCSP request times and client's repeated TCP connection attempts to same IP instead of re-resolving

Initial hypothesis: Split-horizon forwarders in the branch setup returned different TTLs and a subset of resolvers were returning a long-lived cached IP. The control-plane honored the long TTL, attempted TLS resume/OCSP stapling against an endpoint that the egress path no longer serviced properly, and OCSP queries to the intermediate OCSP responder were intermittently blocked/filtered by the branch firewall, causing timeouts and the model artifact pulls to stall.

Immediate customer-facing workaround applied: Customer flushed DNS caches on the branch forwarders, applied a temporary iptables rule to allow OCSP UDP/TCP to the responder, and restarted the artifact-service agent. After the flush and policy change, resolvers returned consistent short TTLs and artifact downloads resumed within ~7 minutes.

Permanent recommendations provided to customer: align TTL settings across split-horizon forwarders, ensure OCSP responder reachability from egress paths, and configure forwarders to respect minimal TTL values and not to serve stale entries after upstream changes.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From branch forwarder A: dig +noall +answer artifact-eu-west.example-s3.internal @10.10.2.2
2) From branch forwarder B: dig +noall +answer artifact-eu-west.example-s3.internal @10.10.3.2
3) Compare TTLs; run sudo tcpdump -i any -s0 -w capture.pcap 'host <artifact-ip> or host <ocsp-responder-ip>' while triggering a model pull; observe repeated connects to same artifact IP and OCSP timeouts.
logs_observations:
Support observed agent logs: "2026-03-12T08:56:02Z artifact-service[pid]: ocsp lookup timeout for responder ocsp.example-ca.org" and "artifact fetch retry (shard 42) to 10.42.11.23". Control-plane trace: "resolver: cached A (ttl=1200) vs resolver B (ttl=30) - choosing cached path". tcpdump shows OCSP requests retransmitted until branch firewall allowed TCP/80 to responder.
Metrics: artifact-fetch-latency spike in dashboard: 08:45-11:15 UTC, 80th percentile token latency +340%.
investigation_notes:
- Support confirmed inconsistent TTLs across the customer's forwarders (10.10.2.2 vs 10.10.3.2).
- SRE noted control-plane used long TTL cache entries and did not immediately re-resolve on OCSP failure; this made the control-plane continue sending requests to an IP that no longer had correct egress path.
- Packet captures showed OCSP responses being dropped by the branch firewall under a default application ACL; customer applied a temporary allow rule for ocsp.example-ca.org.
- No indication of Redwood-side cert or artifact corruption. Artifact integrity checks passed once downloads completed.
- Reproduced locally by simulating split-horizon answers with different TTLs, validating that our resolver library will honor TTLs and will not force immediate re-resolve unless TTL expired or connection fails with cert mismatch.

resolution:
Workaround: Customer flushed branch DNS caches, allowed OCSP responder traffic, and restarted the artifact agent which restored normal artifact pull behavior within ~7 minutes. Root cause: inconsistent split-horizon TTLs combined with branch firewall blocking OCSP traffic caused control-plane to rely on stale cached IP and fail to re-resolve promptly.
Permanent fix / follow-up: Customer will standardize TTLs across forwarders and confirm OCSP/responder reachability from all egress paths. Redwood created INT-4421 to evaluate adding an option to force immediate re-resolve on repeated OCSP failures for VPCE/artifact endpoints. Ticket closed after confirmation from customer that production traffic normalized and no further errors seen for 48 hours.
